messages.subject: Differential analysis question
parts:
Hi Meena and all MSstats developers,
First, thanks for the great series of webinars. I wanted to try the MSstats, again, to include this in our workflows and I came across a potential problem. 
Doing the differential analysis with different software I get a lot of discrepancies and also strange results from MSstats. 


Why are the p-values so strangely aligned on the line? This analysis was done with the Progenesis output. I also used a package SafeQuant https://github.com/eahrne/SafeQuant on the same dataset and I get something completely different. 

I understand that these are different tests: linear model Vs (The summarized peptide/protein expression values are used for statistical testing of between condition differentially abundant peptides/proteins. Here, empirical Bayes moderated t-tests is applied, as implemented in the R/Bioconductor limma package (Smyth, 2004). The resulting per protein and condition comparison p-values are subsequently adjusted for multiple testing using the Benjamini-Hochberg method). 

I included the input files and my script. Can you elaborate on this?

The input file is here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/186w3c-0r0u6kkYaA_aDwzkWZaRmxipjv/view?usp=sharing


Greets
Witek

messages.author: 82f4cbd8cffc3818
messages.subject: Re: Differential analysis question
parts:
Hi Ting

Thank you for looking into this. We've used 3 replicates per group (HEK only, Ecoli spiked in HEK (1:10 (w/w)), Ecoli spiked in HEK (1:20 (w/w))). The expected ratio of Ecoli protein regulation is 2x. Since all Ecoli proteins are expected to be regulated by a factor of 2 we would expect a higher number of significantly regulated with smaller adj.pvalues, as currently observed (similar to the SafeQuant volcano plot in my last post).

                                 ECHigh   ECLow
                    # runs     3             3
     # bioreplicates     3             3      
 # tech. replicates    1              1        

The script I've used:
library(MSstats) #v4.0.0
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

DDinput <- read.csv("DIA-30min_direcDIA_Report_organism.csv")

#convert Spectronaut format to MSstats format
DDraw <- SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(DDinput,
                                    annotation = NULL,
                                    intensity = 'PeakArea',
                                    filter_with_Qvalue = TRUE,
                                    qvalue_cutoff = 0.01,
                                    useUniquePeptide = TRUE,
                                    fewMeasurements="remove",
                                    removeProtein_with1Feature = FALSE,
                                    summaryforMultipleRows=max)   

DDQuantData <- dataProcess(DDraw,
                           normalization='equalizeMedians',
                           summaryMethod="TMP",
                           censoredInt="0",
                           MBimpute=TRUE,

comparison <- MSstatsContrastMatrix("pairwise", c('High Ecoli', 'Low Ecoli', 'HEK'))
DDpairwiseComparison <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix=comparison, data=DDQuantData)

#add species information
DD_pwcomp <- with(DDpairwiseComparison,ComparisonResult)
DD_pwcomp$species <- DDinput$PG.Organisms[match(DD_pwcomp$Protein, DDinput$PG.ProteinGroups)]
DD_pwcomp <- DD_pwcomp %>% mutate(species = ifelse(grepl("Escherichia", species),"ecoli", ifelse(grepl("Homo", species),"human","unknown")))

#volcano plot
DD_pwcomp %>% filter(!is.na(Protein),Label == "High Ecoli vs Low Ecoli") %>%
  ggplot(., aes(x=log2FC, y=-log10(adj.pvalue), col=species)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-8,4),breaks=c(-8, -4, 0, 4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,7),breaks=c(0, 2, 4, 6)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggtitle("High Ecoli vs Low Ecoli (MSstats)") +
  geom_vline(xintercept=c(-1, 1), col="red", linetype="dotted") +
  geom_hline(yintercept=-log10(0.05), col="red", linetype="dotted")

I'm also happy to share the dataset on which this analysis is based in case this is of any help...

Thank you already in advance for your help!

Kind regards,
Christian

On Tuesday, June 15, 2021 at 10:59:02 AM UTC-4 c.sc...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi Ting

Thank you for looking into this. We've used 3 replicates per group (HEK only, Ecoli spiked in HEK (1:10 (w/w)), Ecoli spiked in HEK (1:20 (w/w))). The expected ratio of Ecoli protein regulation is 2x. Since all Ecoli proteins are expected to be regulated by a factor of 2 we would expect a higher number of significantly regulated with smaller adj.pvalues, as currently observed (similar to the SafeQuant volcano plot in my last post).

                                 ECHigh   ECLow
                    # runs     3             3
     # bioreplicates     3             3      
 # tech. replicates    1              1        

The script I've used:
library(MSstats) #v4.0.0
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

DDinput <- read.csv("DIA-30min_direcDIA_Report_organism.csv")

#convert Spectronaut format to MSstats format
DDraw <- SpectronauttoMSstatsFormat(DDinput,
                                    annotation = NULL,
                                    intensity = 'PeakArea',
                                    filter_with_Qvalue = TRUE,
                                    qvalue_cutoff = 0.01,
                                    useUniquePeptide = TRUE,
                                    fewMeasurements="remove",
                                    removeProtein_with1Feature = FALSE,
                                    summaryforMultipleRows=max)   

DDQuantData <- dataProcess(DDraw,
                           normalization='equalizeMedians',
                           summaryMethod="TMP",
                           censoredInt="0",
                           MBimpute=TRUE,

comparison <- MSstatsContrastMatrix("pairwise", c('High Ecoli', 'Low Ecoli', 'HEK'))
DDpairwiseComparison <- groupComparison(contrast.matrix=comparison, data=DDQuantData)

#add species information
DD_pwcomp <- with(DDpairwiseComparison,ComparisonResult)
DD_pwcomp$species <- DDinput$PG.Organisms[match(DD_pwcomp$Protein, DDinput$PG.ProteinGroups)]
DD_pwcomp <- DD_pwcomp %>% mutate(species = ifelse(grepl("Escherichia", species),"ecoli", ifelse(grepl("Homo", species),"human","unknown")))

#volcano plot
DD_pwcomp %>% filter(!is.na(Protein),Label == "High Ecoli vs Low Ecoli") %>%
  ggplot(., aes(x=log2FC, y=-log10(adj.pvalue), col=species)) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.4) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(-8,4),breaks=c(-8, -4, 0, 4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,7),breaks=c(0, 2, 4, 6)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  ggtitle("High Ecoli vs Low Ecoli (MSstats)") +
  geom_vline(xintercept=c(-1, 1), col="red", linetype="dotted") +
  geom_hline(yintercept=-log10(0.05), col="red", linetype="dotted")

I'm also happy to share the dataset on which this analysis is based in case this is of any help...

Thank you already in advance for your help!

Kind regards,
Christian

choimee...@gmail.com schrieb am Dienstag, 11. Mai 2021 um 21:58:56 UTC+2:
there are big changes of models between v2 and v3. We found that models in v2 have many false positives and potentially overfitted in many cases. We proposed the new models in v3 (under the revision). Now, v3 has fewer significant proteins. But, we confirmed that v3 doesn't lose TP and it has much better performance in terms of TP, FP, PPV. 
If the number of bio replicate is small (less than 3 per group) and data has bigger variation, MSstats might not report significant proteins.

HTH
- Meena
